question: Can the decoded AprilTag ID tell the markers apart?
finding: No. Both decode tag36h11 ID 0 (113,852 valid rows; code assertion EXPECTED_TAG={0,0,0}). The machine ID alone does not distinguish them; camera identity and the handwritten labels do.
manuscript_implication: State that both markers decode as AprilTag ID 0. Never write "tag 1"/"tag 2" or use the decoded ID to name markers.

question: Is there measured evidence that bears on MK05?
finding: Yes, indirect and consistent with the owner decision. At the torsion line, vertical amplitude divided by in-plane roll gives an apparent distance from the rotation axis: cam1 median 127.0 mm (range 117.9-134.5), cam2 125.4 mm (116.6-132.5), cam3 5.9 mm (1.4-14.2), six conditions (90, 140, 160, 180, 200, 220 RPM). All three cameras report the same roll within 2% (cam2/cam1 1.014, cam3/cam1 1.009). The laser centre head sits on the rotation axis (S5a addendum).
status: INFERRED (data-derived estimate; assumes rigid rotation about a fixed axis; drifts with RPM; carries the 2.5% tag-size scale bound)
sources: results/s4_roll_and_lever_arm_at_torsion_line.csv columns lever_cam1_mm, lever_cam2_mm, lever_cam3_mm; docs/gates/S4.md result notes; docs/gates/S5a.md ADDENDUM 2026-10-16
manuscript_implication: This measures distance from the rotation axis, not the separation between the markers. Quote only as an estimate.

question: Is any lever-arm distance verified?
finding: No. About 125 mm (cam1/cam2) and about 6 mm (cam3) are data-derived estimates from six conditions. The 135.14 mm marker separation is RETRACTED (2024 photograph, different geometry); 200 mm is an unverified report. A surveyed 2025 marker separation does not exist. cam1/cam2 vertical metric motion includes the lever-arm x roll term and is not direct heave.
sources: docs/gates/S4.md; docs/reference_audit/NOTES.md F13; 14_..._REPORT.md "Why this matters" and "What remains unresolved" item 4; 13_..._CSV row 8 (RETRACTED); PER_CAMERA_RMS_GO_NO_GO.md condition 4
manuscript_implication: Quote as "approximately 125 mm, estimated from the data, not surveyed" or omit. Never quote 135.14 mm. Never call cam1/cam2 H1,y direct heave.
